# How to Import a Book from gutenberg.org

```{r}
#| label: gutenberg-demo
url  <- "https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/84/pg84.txt"
text <- readLines(url, encoding = "UTF-8") |> paste(collapse = "\n")
cat(substr(text, 1, 500))
```

---

# Setup: Books and Tokenizer

```{r}
#| label: books-and-tokenizer
baseurl <- "https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/"

books <- data.frame(
  code  = c("84", "64317", "11",   "1513",       "76",
            "219",         "2591",       "2148",          "36",           "829"),
  title = c("Frankenstein", "GreatGatsby", "AliceWonderland", "RomeoJuliet", "HuckFinn",
            "HeartDarkness", "GrimmsTales", "EdgarAllenPoe", "WarOfTheWorlds", "GulliversTravels")
)

# Load GPT-2 tokenizer (downloads vocab on first run)
gpt2 <- tok::tokenizer$from_pretrained("gpt2")
```

---

# Part 1: Total Characters, Words, and Tokens

```{r}
#| label: part1-counts
#| cache: true
results <- vector("list", nrow(books))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(books))) {
  fullurl <- paste0(baseurl, books$code[i], "/pg", books$code[i], ".txt")
  text    <- readLines(fullurl, encoding = "UTF-8") |> paste(collapse = "\n")

  results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    title   = books$title[i],
    n_chars = nchar(text),
    n_words = length(strsplit(trimws(text), "\\s+")[[1]]),
    n_token = length(gpt2$encode(text)$ids)
  )
}

counts <- bind_rows(results)
counts
```

---

# Part 2: Unique and Total Counts

```{r}
#| label: part2-unique
#| cache: true
full_results <- vector("list", nrow(books))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(books))) {
  fullurl <- paste0(baseurl, books$code[i], "/pg", books$code[i], ".txt")
  text    <- readLines(fullurl, encoding = "UTF-8") |> paste(collapse = "\n")

  chars  <- strsplit(text, "")[[1]]
  words  <- strsplit(trimws(text), "\\s+")[[1]]
  tokens <- gpt2$encode(text)$ids

  full_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    title        = books$title[i],
    total_chars  = length(chars),
    unique_chars = length(unique(chars)),
    total_words  = length(words),
    unique_words = length(unique(words)),
    total_token  = length(tokens),
    unique_token = length(unique(tokens))
  )
}

full_counts <- bind_rows(full_results)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-part2
#| fig-cap: "Total (A) and unique (B) counts across tokenization schemes for 10 Project Gutenberg books."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

# Reshape to long format for plotting
long_counts <- full_counts |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -title,
    names_to  = c("measure", "scheme"),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    scheme  = factor(tools::toTitleCase(scheme), levels = c("Chars", "Words", "Token")),
    measure = if_else(measure == "total", "A) Total", "B) Unique")
  )

ggplot(long_counts, aes(x = scheme, y = count)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.08, size = 2.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6,
               linewidth = 0.8, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_scientific()) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

---

# Part 3: Unique by Total Counts

```{r}
#| label: fig-part3
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between unique and total counts for each tokenization scheme across 10 books."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.5

# Build a long frame with both total and unique per scheme
scatter_data <- full_counts |>
  select(title,
         chars_total  = total_chars,  chars_unique  = unique_chars,
         words_total  = total_words,  words_unique  = unique_words,
         token_total  = total_token,  token_unique  = unique_token) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -title,
    names_to  = c("scheme", "measure"),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(scheme = factor(tools::toTitleCase(scheme),
                         levels = c("Chars", "Words", "Token")))

# Compute per-scheme correlation labels
cor_labels <- scatter_data |>
  group_by(scheme) |>
  summarise(r = cor(unique, total), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("r = %.2f", r))

ggplot(scatter_data, aes(x = unique, y = total)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = cor_labels, aes(label = label),
            x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.2, vjust = 1.5,
            fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_scientific()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_scientific()) +
  facet_wrap(~ scheme, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Unique", y = "Total") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r}
#| label: outlier
# Which book has the most unique characters?
full_counts |>
  slice_max(unique_chars, n = 1) |>
  select(title, unique_chars)
```
